scene_0_morning_brief.speaker: Rose
scene_0_morning_brief.text: Seven means ready at seven. We're going out of town today. The weavers.

scene_0_morning_brief.speaker: Lola Susan
scene_0_morning_brief.text: Manang Loleng is expecting you. Be polite, and don't touch the looms unless she says.

scene_0_morning_brief.speaker: Lola Jonabel
scene_0_morning_brief.text: \Piña… My lola used to weave, you know. Every afternoon, under the house. The sound of it put me to sleep.

scene_0_morning_brief.speaker: Lola Jonabel
scene_0_morning_brief.text: I'd forgotten I remembered. Go. Tell me everything tonight.

scene_0_morning_brief.speaker: Rose
scene_0_morning_brief.text: \Hinay-hinay, Lola. We'll be back before dark. Stay close, balikbayan.
scene_0_morning_brief.translation: Take it slow, Lola. We'll be back before dark. Stay close, balikbayan.

scene_1_hear_the_looms.speaker: Rose
scene_1_hear_the_looms.text: Hear that? That's the looms. Come on, inside.

scene_1_arrival_at_the_loom_house.speaker: Manang Loleng
scene_1_arrival_at_the_loom_house.translation: Come in, visitors! Look at our weaving.

scene_1_arrival_at_the_loom_house.speaker: Player
scene_1_arrival_at_the_loom_house.text: Whoa. Amazing, Grandma — I mean, Manang. Sorry, it's my first time seeing a loom like this.

scene_1_arrival_at_the_loom_house.speaker: Manang Loleng
scene_1_arrival_at_the_loom_house.translation: No problem. Many visitors are amazed here too.

scene_1_arrival_at_the_loom_house.speaker: Rose
scene_1_arrival_at_the_loom_house.text: This whole community weaves piña cloth. Been doing it for generations — older than any of us.

scene_1_arrival_at_the_loom_house.speaker: Manang Loleng
scene_1_arrival_at_the_loom_house.translation: This comes from over there, the farm, from the piña plant. There's still a lot of work needed before it becomes cloth.

questions.question: "Halin ra igto sa taeamnan." What is "taeamnan"?

scene_1_arrival_at_the_loom_house.speaker: Manang Loleng
scene_1_arrival_at_the_loom_house.text: So, apo? What do you think of it?

choices.label: This is beautiful work, Manang. I'd love to learn more.
It's really intricate, kind of hard to understand all at once.
This looks like it takes forever, isn't a machine faster?

scene_1_arrival_at_the_loom_house.speaker: Manang Loleng
scene_1_arrival_at_the_loom_house.text: \Saeamat, \apo. Not many young ones say that anymore.

scene_1_arrival_at_the_loom_house.speaker: Manang Loleng
scene_1_arrival_at_the_loom_house.text: Step by step. Even I took years.

scene_1_arrival_at_the_loom_house.speaker: Manang Loleng
scene_1_arrival_at_the_loom_house.text: Machines can't feel the thread the way a hand does. That's the difference.

scene_1_arrival_at_the_loom_house.speaker: Manang Loleng
scene_1_arrival_at_the_loom_house.translation: Do you want to try making it? Here, follow me.

scene_2_trying_the_loom.speaker: Rose
scene_2_trying_the_loom.text: Oh, this I have to see. Balikbayan versus loom. Place your bets.

scene_2_trying_the_loom.speaker: Player
scene_2_trying_the_loom.text: Gee, thanks for the confidence, Rose.

scene_2_trying_the_loom.speaker: Manang Loleng
scene_2_trying_the_loom.translation: Slower, that's all. This isn't a race.

scene_2_trying_the_loom.text: Will you try weaving on your own?

choices.label: I'll take it slow, Manang. Show me the first move again.
Can you guide my hands through it first?
Maybe I'll just watch, this looks too hard for me.

scene_2_trying_the_loom.speaker: Manang Loleng
scene_2_trying_the_loom.text: That's the spirit, \apo. One thread at a time.

scene_2_trying_the_loom.speaker: Rose
scene_2_trying_the_loom.text: Come on, at least try one row. I'll laugh either way, might as well earn it.
Manang Loleng calls out a thread colour. Trace its letters on the loom before the shuttle crosses.

scene_2_trying_the_loom.speaker: Manang Loleng
scene_2_trying_the_loom.translation: Oh, good! For a first piece of work, that'll do.

scene_2_trying_the_loom.speaker: Rose
scene_2_trying_the_loom.text: …Okay. I lost the bet. Don't let it go to your head.

scene_2_trying_the_loom.speaker: Manang Loleng
scene_2_trying_the_loom.translation: You know, my first weaving was worse than that.

scene_2_trying_the_loom.speaker: Rose
scene_2_trying_the_loom.text: I'd have laughed, but… honestly, mine was worse too. Want another go?

scene_3_closing_gift.speaker: Manang Loleng
scene_3_closing_gift.translation: Here, take this. A token from our community.

scene_3_closing_gift.speaker: Manang Loleng
scene_3_closing_gift.translation: For your books, and so that you won't forget us.

scene_3_closing_gift.speaker: Manang Loleng
scene_3_closing_gift.translation: Take care on your trip. Come back when you have time.

scene_3_closing_gift.speaker: Rose
scene_3_closing_gift.text: Not bad for a field trip, balikbayan. Two down, more to go.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_verbs_.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_verbs_.text: \Tan-awa \sanda. \Panaw — to walk… wait, save that one. \Bangon — to get up, like when you fall.
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_verbs_.translation: Look at them. Panaw — to walk… wait, save that one. Bangon — to get up, like when you fall.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_verbs_.speaker: Player
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_verbs_.text: These make sense with the actions right in front of us.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_verbs_.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_verbs_.text: That's the point. Now, getting around.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_verbs_.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_verbs_.text: Refill. Your treat, balikbayan. First, words.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_verbs_.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_verbs_.text: \Maliya — come here. \Agto — go. \Igto — there. \Diretso — straight. \Liko — turn. \Tuo — right. \Waea — left. \Dayon — then, or “continue.”

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_verbs_.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_verbs_.text: \Bakae — to buy. \Baligya — to sell. \Tan-aw — to look, to see. \Hambae — to speak. \Sabát — to answer.
Will you try using the new words?

choices.label: I'll try — “Gusto ko mag bakae,” I want to buy? Something like that?
I get the meanings, but it's still hard to use them correctly.
There are too many verbs now, I'm losing track.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_verbs_.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_verbs_.text: Close enough! You're building sentences now, not just words.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_verbs_.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_verbs_.text: That's normal. Meaning first, grammar later.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_verbs_.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_verbs_.text: Deep breath. We'll circle back to these. No rush.

questions.question: The visitor gives money for a coffee. What are they doing?
The barista hands over the cup for money. What is she doing?
Rose asks you something. What do you do?

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_verbs_.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_verbs_.text: Not bad. You were watching.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_verbs_.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_verbs_.text: Almost. Watch the counter: someone's always doing \bakae or \baligya there.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_verbs_.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_verbs_.text: \Taas — tall, or long. \Naba — short. \Paspas — fast. \Hinay — slow. Manang's “\hinayi” means slower, and “\hinay-hinay” means little by little.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_verbs_.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_verbs_.text: \Bug-at — heavy. \Maugan — light, not bug-at. Small words, but you'll need them everywhere.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_verbs_.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_verbs_.text: \Kuntra naman — “against.” Rarely used, but good to know.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_verbs_.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_verbs_.text: Okay, match them up. Word to meaning.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_verbs_.speaker: Player
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_verbs_.text: My head's kind of full now, but I think I actually get most of it.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_verbs_.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_verbs_.text: That's the goal. Not perfect. Just moving forward.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_verbs_.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_verbs_.text: And \panaw? To walk. Told you I'd save it. Let's \panaw home, balikbayan.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_verbs_.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_verbs_.text: \Agto \igto sa counter, \diretso kat \sangkiri, tapos \liko \pa \tuo.
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_verbs_.translation: Go there to the counter, straight for a little bit, then turn to the right.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_verbs_.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_verbs_.text: See? You didn't even need a map.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_verbs_.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_verbs_.text: \Maliya! \Liko sa \waea, \dayon \diretso.
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_verbs_.translation: Come here! Turn left, then straight.

scene_4_leg1_hint.speaker: Rose
scene_4_leg1_hint.text: \Tuo! Your other right, balikbayan. Straight up a little, then turn right to the counter.

scene_4_leg2_hint.speaker: Rose
scene_4_leg2_hint.text: \Waea, balikbayan. Turn left, then straight down to the table.

scene_5_the_sound_of_the_loom.speaker: Lola Susan
scene_5_the_sound_of_the_loom.text: There they are. Did you behave, Rose?

scene_5_the_sound_of_the_loom.speaker: Rose
scene_5_the_sound_of_the_loom.text: I always behave. Ask the balikbayan how the loom went.

scene_5_the_sound_of_the_loom.speaker: Player
scene_5_the_sound_of_the_loom.text: I wove a row. A very crooked row.

scene_5_the_sound_of_the_loom.speaker: Player
scene_5_the_sound_of_the_loom.text: I wove a whole row. Rose lost a bet.

scene_5_the_sound_of_the_loom.speaker: Player
scene_5_the_sound_of_the_loom.text: Manang Loleng gave me this. I thought you should see it.

scene_5_the_sound_of_the_loom.speaker: Lola Jonabel
scene_5_the_sound_of_the_loom.text: My lola made one just like this for my missal. I lost it when we moved to America. Fifty years ago.
Lola Jonabel holds the bookmark out to give it back.

choices.label: Keep it, Lola. It's yours now.
Can we share it? I'll leave it in your missal.

scene_5_the_sound_of_the_loom.speaker: Lola Jonabel
scene_5_the_sound_of_the_loom.text: \Saeamat, \apo. Now I'll hear the loom when I read.

scene_5_the_sound_of_the_loom.speaker: Lola Jonabel
scene_5_the_sound_of_the_loom.text: Good. Use it. And go back and see her one day.

scene_5_the_sound_of_the_loom.speaker: Rose
scene_5_the_sound_of_the_loom.text: Okay, that's enough feelings for one day. Sleep, balikbayan. Tomorrow's mud.

scene_loleng_habi_habi.speaker: Manang Loleng
scene_loleng_habi_habi.text: Back at the loom, \apo? I call the words, you weave them. \Hinay-hinay first, then \paspas.

scene_loleng_habi_habi.speaker: Manang Loleng
scene_loleng_habi_habi.text: \Hinay-hinay, \apo. The loom will wait for you.

scene_revisit_arrival.speaker: Rose
scene_revisit_arrival.text: Go on, Manang Loleng's inside. I'll wait out here. Talk to me when you want to head home.

culture_gallery_curator.speaker: Gallery Curator
culture_gallery_curator.text: Welcome to the gallery! Everything you see here starts as a pineapple leaf. \Piña.

culture_gallery_curator.speaker: Gallery Curator
culture_gallery_curator.text: First we scrape the leaf with a shard of porcelain. That gives the rough fiber, the bastos.

culture_gallery_curator.speaker: Gallery Curator
culture_gallery_curator.text: Then a coconut shell draws out the finest fiber, the liniwan. That is what becomes the softest cloth.

culture_gallery_curator.speaker: Gallery Curator
culture_gallery_curator.text: In 2023, UNESCO listed Aklan piña handloom weaving as Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. The first from the Visayas!

culture_gallery_curator.speaker: Gallery Curator
culture_gallery_curator.text: You'll see piña in a barong at a wedding, or a gown for a big day. Look around, take your time.

examine_fiber_jars.text: Two jars of fiber. One is bastos: rough and stiff. The other is liniwan: fine and shiny, almost like silk.

examine_scraping_tools.text: A porcelain shard and half a coconut shell, both worn smooth from years of scraping leaves.

examine_pina_barong.text: A piña barong, thin enough to see through, embroidered by hand. A card says it was made for a wedding.

examine_unesco_frame.text: A framed notice: Aklan Piña Handloom Weaving, inscribed by UNESCO on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity, December 2023.

lines.speaker: Lola Jonabel
lines.text: I read with Manang Loleng's bookmark every night, \apo. I can almost hear the loom.

lines.speaker: Lola Jonabel
lines.text: Are you using Manang Loleng's bookmark, \apo? Good. And go and see her again one day.

lines.speaker: Lola Susan
lines.text: Rose says you wove a whole row at Manang Loleng's loom. She didn't even complain about it.

lines.speaker: Lola Susan
lines.text: A crooked first row? Don't worry. Rose's first row at that loom was worse, and she was ten.

lines.speaker: Nong Pedring
lines.text: You went to the weavers in Haboean, \apo? Manang Loleng's \piña is the best in all of Aklan.
